source.label: The electrical flow fails above exponent two

reviewer: Claude Code with sole fresh-context medium reviewer

claims.summary: For L > 0, s = L sqrt(log N/N), eps in (0, 1/2], grids of k x k cells of side delta = 1/k with delta <= N^(-eps) and N delta^2 >= 1 (the reduction's grids, delta <= s/32 and N delta^2 >= 16 log N, among them for every eps < 1/2), X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform with cell counts n_Q, the electrical flow theta (least squares, unit conductances on the cell graph, outflow n_Q - N delta^2), K' >= 1, lambda' in [N/K', K'N] and a coordinate j with alpha_j in (2, infinity], or alpha_j = 2 when L < sqrt(eps)/(pi^2 K') (logarithms natural): for every C > 0 there is c(C, L, K', eps, alpha_j) > 0 with P(lambda' delta^2 sum over edges e of coordinate j of psi_alpha_j(|theta_e|/(delta lambda' s)) > C N) >= c for all large N. So the electrical flow's flow-bound value is not O(N) with probability tending to one at any pair of the curve, nor is that of any finite sequence of divisible-sandpile stages with equal splitting on the cell graph carrying the counts to N delta^2, which is the same flow. Per-edge variance: N delta^2 ||w_e||^2 with ||w_e||^2 >= ln k/(2 pi^4) on a fraction about 8/pi^7 of the edges (free-boundary spectral sum). Uses the imported Berry-Esseen theorem.
claims.assessment: Working proof: theta_e is an i.i.d. sum of w_e(Q(X_i)) with |w_e| <= 1 (acyclic unit flows); an exact free-boundary spectral sum bounds the mean of ||w_e||^2 over edges below by ln k/pi^4 and every one above by (pi^3/16) ln k + 6; Berry-Esseen gives each good edge a Gaussian tail of normalized spread at least sqrt(eps/(2 pi^4))/(K' L); a reverse Markov step on the exceeding fraction gives probability bounded below; psi_alpha with alpha > 2 beats the Gaussian tail. A numerical check of the spectral bounds at k = 8..128 is in research/results/ultimate_matching_electrical_flow_20261017/spectral-check.txt.
claims.rationale: Excludes the electrical flow, and through lem:idle-slack-sandpile and lem:balanced-sandpile-flow every equal-splitting sandpile sequence, from the flow route at every pair of the curve; the cheapest flow, flows with circulations added and state-dependent sandpiles are not covered.
claims.next_action: Nearest-midline exits are median cuts with target 1/2, in the class of thm:split-matched-transport-obstruction with A = 1/2; decide whether the exit matching, which moves only the crossing points, stays within m/(18 sqrt(Gamma N)) of the transport T, which stretches every point by about |c - 1/2| l per level, or whether the theorem's walk tolerates that predictable difference.

relationships: Its sandpile clause identifies the sandpile sequences' net flow with the electrical flow.
Equal splitting on the cell grid gives unit conductances, so the sandpile flow is this electrical flow.
The same failure for the dyadic flow, with probability tending to one; its proof does not apply to the electrical flow.
Its part (c) supplies the grids and the flow-bound value.
